prompts.instruction: Read the text and choose the label that best fits the supplied definitions of not_depression and depression. Focus on evidence relevant to those definitions; do not infer depression merely from a mention of another mental health condition.
Compare the text with the supplied label definitions and choose the best fitting label. Strictly follow the label definitions.
Evaluate the post as a whole, considering its context, emotional expressions, and temporal information. Avoid making classification decisions based solely on isolated words or phrases.

Identify the evidence in the post that supports each applicable label and select the label with the strongest textual support. Do not assume symptoms or experiences that are not supported by the text.

Carefully distinguish between not_depression and depression using the supplied definitions. When the text appears to match both categories, compare the relevant criteria and select the single best-supported label.

Classify the post strictly according to the provided label definitions. Do not automatically assign depression based on negative emotions, emotional intensity, or general psychological distress alone.

Evaluate the evidence for both labels before making a decision. Select depression when the text provides evidence matching its supplied definition; compare that evidence with the not_depression criteria and choose the best-supported label.

Distinguish depression from not_depression using the supplied definitions. Consider fluctuations in emotional state, periods of improvement, and expressions of hope as specified by the depression criteria; do not treat hope or improvement alone as proof of not_depression.

Distinguish depression-related evidence from temporary negative emotions, situational distress, and discussions about other people's experiences. Apply the not_depression criteria whenever the post matches those definitions, even if negative emotional language is present.

Compare the post with each label definition separately. Identify which criteria are directly supported by the text, avoid unsupported assumptions, and select the label with the strongest overall match rather than the most emotionally intense label.
